holidays.name: Bubble Bath Day
holidays.description: Fill the tub, pour in way too much foam, and sink into a cloud of bubbles. It's the official excuse to soak away the January chill and treat bath time as a serious wellness ritual.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a cozy fixture of the early-January calendar, when many people are craving warmth and self-care.
holidays.funFact: Bubbles form because soap molecules sit at the surface of the water and trap air inside thin films. That's why a bath gets fluffier the harder the water splashes in.

holidays.name: Earth's Rotation Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate that the ground under your feet is spinning. It honors the moment science showed our planet turns on its axis, so go ahead and feel a little dizzy.
holidays.origin: It commemorates January 8, 1851, when French physicist Léon Foucault began his famous pendulum demonstration of Earth's rotation. He used a swinging pendulum to show the rotation, and the gyroscope got its name from his work soon afterward.
holidays.funFact: Foucault's pendulum appears to change its swing direction over the day. In fact the pendulum keeps swinging the same way while the Earth rotates beneath it.

holidays.name: National Snuggle a Chicken Day
holidays.description: A feathery celebration for backyard flocks and the people who love them. Scoop up a chicken, give it a gentle cuddle, and discover why hens make surprisingly soothing companions.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It likely grew out of the backyard chicken-keeping boom, with fans who treat their hens as pets.
holidays.funFact: Many chickens go calm and sleepy when held securely and stroked gently, and some even seem to enjoy lap time.
